body.statement:
For every measurable endpoint selection \(g\in\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), there is one full-data law \(P^g\in\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) such that
\[
\tau^{P^g}=g\qquad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The completion preserves the entire observed law and remains legal on every zero-capacity contact set.
body.proof_tex:
Choose a measurable representative of \(g\in\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), put \(c_z=b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}\), and define
\[
f^g_{1,z}(r)=[g_z(r)-c_z(r)]_+,\qquad
f^g_{0,z}(r)=[c_z(r)-g_z(r)]_+.
\tag{1}
\]
The box inequalities give, \(P_X\)-almost surely,
\[
0\leq f^g_{a,z}(r)\leq u_{a,z}(r),\qquad
f^g_{1,z}(r)-f^g_{0,z}(r)=g_z(r)-c_z(r).
\tag{2}
\]
Modify the representative on a \(P_X\)-null set so that (2) holds everywhere on the fixed version used in the Wang-class definition, and set
\[
q^g_{a,z}(r)=
\begin{cases}
f^g_{a,z}(r)/u_{a,z}(r),&u_{a,z}(r)>0,\\
0,&u_{a,z}(r)=0.
\end{cases}
\tag{3}
\]
Division occurs only on the positive-capacity set.  On the zero-capacity set, (2) forces \(f^g_{a,z}=0\).  Hence \(0\leq q^g_{a,z}\leq1\).

Start from the zero-residual completion in the established completion-witness lemma.  The zero family is feasible, so that lemma and the completion-law definition supply \(P^0\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) with armwise pairs
\[
\widetilde T_a^0=\min\{T^0(a),C^0(a)\},\qquad
\Delta_a^0=\mathbf 1\{C^0(a)\leq T^0(a)\},
\tag{4}
\]
whose conditional law given \(X\) is the observed arm-\(a\) law.  On a product extension, draw independent \(U_0,U_1\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), independently of all variables under \(P^0\), and set
\[
T^g(a)=
\begin{cases}
t_{\max},&\Delta_a^0=1\text{ and }U_a\leq q^g_{a,Z}(R),\\
\widetilde T_a^0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad C^g(a)=C^0(a).
\tag{5}
\]
Under the zero completion, \(C^0(a)=t_{\max}+1\) on \(\{\Delta_a^0=0\}\), whereas \(C^0(a)=\widetilde T_a^0\) on \(\{\Delta_a^0=1\}\).  Hence (5) leaves the observed pair exactly equal to \((\widetilde T_a^0,\Delta_a^0)\).  On dropout records, either \(T^g(a)=t_{\max}\geq C^g(a)\) or \(T^g(a)=C^g(a)=\widetilde T_a^0\), and the tie convention records both as dropout.  On uncensored records, \(T^g(a)=\widetilde T_a^0<C^g(a)\).  Thus the observed law remains \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(0\leq T^g(a)\leq t_{\max}\).

The zero completion makes \(A\) conditionally independent of the armwise potential vector given \(X\).  The uniforms are conditionally independent of \(A\), and (5) is a measurable transformation using \(X\), that vector, and the uniforms.  Therefore \(T^g(a)\perp\!\!\!\perp A\mid X\).  Treatment overlap is the protocol overlap, and censoring overlap is unchanged with the observed law.  Assigning \((T,C)=(T^g(A),C^g(A))\) gives consistency.  The resulting law \(P^g\) therefore belongs to \(\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).

Conditional independence of \(U_a\), together with (3)--(5), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{P^g}[(T^g(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]
&=q^g_{a,z}(r)
E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[(t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\\
&=q^g_{a,z}(r)u_{a,z}(r)
=f^g_{a,z}(r).
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
On \(\{u_{a,z}=0\}\), the last equality is \(0=0\); elsewhere it follows from the legitimate division in (3).  Conditional treatment exchangeability and consistency yield
\[
E_{P^g}[T^g(a)\mid Z=z,R=r]=b_{a,z}(r)+f^g_{a,z}(r).
\tag{7}
\]
Subtracting (7) between arms and applying (2) proves
\[
\tau_z^{P^g}(r)=c_z(r)+f^g_{1,z}(r)-f^g_{0,z}(r)=g_z(r)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\]
This proves simultaneous attainability.
body.justification: The measurable extension of the armwise completion proves converse attainability for the full Wang-compatible image, including zero-capacity contacts.
body.gap: The frozen continuous completion proves attainability only in the continuous slice and therefore cannot alone establish the full measurable image modulo null sets.
body.consumer: The Wang-compatible box-sharpness theorem uses this completion for its reverse inclusion.
